facts.text: The live feed caps its strip at MAX_ROWS of 80 rows, and trim pops the oldest rows past that cap.
SNIPPET_MAX is 90, and snippet replaces a longer value with a cut copy ending in a single ellipsis character.
TICK_MS is 10000, the interval at which mount re-renders the relative times of the feed rows.
text returns an empty string for undefined or null and String of the value for everything else.
at: return value === undefined || value === null ? '' : String(value);

facts.text: snippet collapses every run of whitespace to one space and trims both ends before it measures the length.
snippet returns the literal (empty) when the collapsed text is falsy.
place falls back to the subject_id and then to the constant the graph when a row has no subject_name.
lineFor renders a subjects insert as new subject followed by the name, the id or (unnamed subject).
For a facts insert lineFor prefixes the snippet with the actor and the word added only when row.actor is non-empty.
at: return who ? who + ' added ' + what + ' to ' + where : 'new fact ' + what + ' in ' + where;

facts.text: A facts delete renders as the snippet, the word deleted and in, then the place.
at: if (row.op === 'delete') return what + ' deleted in ' + where;

facts.text: For any other table lineFor falls back to the table name, the op name and in the place.
ago returns just now when the elapsed time is under 5 seconds.
ago rounds the elapsed time to whole seconds and appends s ago for anything under 60 seconds.
ago returns an empty string when Date.parse fails on the timestamp, which it tests with isFinite.
mount sets reduced from matchMedia on the prefers-reduced-motion: reduce query, which skips the new-row animation.
The feed list gets role log and an explicit aria-live of off so one batch of rows does not interrupt a screen reader.
mount starts setInterval(tick, TICK_MS) only when window.setInterval is a function.
mount returns an object that exposes ingest, reset and destroy.
at: return { ingest: ingest, reset: reset, destroy: destroy };

facts.text: The Activity toggle button flips collapsed and mirrors the new state in aria-expanded.
mount starts by emptying the host element with host.textContent.
mount takes an optional now function from options, defaulting to Date.now.
at: var now = typeof options.now === 'function' ? options.now : function () { return Date.now(); };

facts.text: ingest skips any change whose seq is not finite or is not greater than lastSeen, treating it as a redelivery.
ingest sorts the accepted changes by seq ascending before it builds any line.
ingest advances lastSeen to the seq of the final change in the sorted batch.
ingest skips refs and slots rows when it builds one line per change.
ingest drops a facts update whose fact_status is superseded when the same batch inserted that fact.
Refs that name no fact on screen collapse into one line reading plus the count and refs in the place.
at: base: '+' + loose + ' refs in ' + (looseWhere || 'the graph'), refs: 0, text: '',

facts.text: ingest attaches the new lines in ascending seq order, so the newest row ends up first.
at: for (k = 0; k < lines.length; k++) attach(lines[k], at);

facts.text: ingest returns without touching the DOM when no change survives the watermark check.
A ref that names a fact line already on screen increments that line's refs count instead of adding a row.
attach gives a row the f-row class and adds f-new only when the entry is fresh and motion is allowed.
at: var li = el('li', null, null, entry.fresh && !reduced ? 'f-row f-new' : 'f-row');

facts.text: attach prepends the new li ahead of list.firstChild.
attach records the entry in factIndex under its factId when the entry has one.
trim deletes the factIndex entry of a dropped row only when the index still points at that same entry.
renderAll rebuilds every row with the f-row class and never re-adds f-new.
at: var li = el('li', null, list, 'f-row'); // the f-new class belongs to the batch that added it

facts.text: renderAll returns immediately once destroyed is set.
tick rewrites only the time span text of each row and rebuilds nothing else.
reset empties rows, clears factIndex and sets lastSeen back to -1.
destroy sets destroyed and clears the stored timer through win.clearInterval.
el writes the text prop through textContent and passes every other prop to setAttribute.
at: if (k === "text") node.textContent = props[k]; else node.setAttribute(k, props[k]);

facts.text: api parses the response body as JSON first and throws the body error message, or r.statusText, when r.ok is false.
at: if (!r.ok) throw new Error(body.error ? body.error.message : r.statusText);

facts.text: clear replaces the children of main through main.replaceChildren.
factRow links the fact id to the #/fact/ route with the id passed through encodeURIComponent.
home loads its subject list from the /api/subjects endpoint.
search requests /api/search with the q parameter passed through encodeURIComponent.
subject requests /api/compile with the subject id passed through encodeURIComponent.
A keydown of Enter in the search box with a non-empty trimmed value sets the hash to #/search/ plus the encoded query.
subject appends a note paragraph with the gaps JSON only when d.gaps is non-empty.
at: if (d.gaps && d.gaps.length) nodes.push(el("p", { class: "note", text: "gaps: " + JSON.stringify(d.gaps) }));

facts.text: subject ends the page with a Raw heading and the whole response through JSON.stringify with an indent of 2 spaces.
at: nodes.push(el("h2", { text: "Raw" }), el("pre", { text: JSON.stringify(d, null, 2) }));

facts.text: home offers a Graph (subject tree) link that points at the #/graph/ route.
at: clear(el("h2", { text: "Subjects" }), el("p", null, link("Graph (subject tree)", "#/graph/")), list);

facts.text: fact requests /api/fact with the id passed through encodeURIComponent.
Each ref line shows the rel, the kind and the basis of that reference inside parentheses.
Only a ref whose kind is fact becomes a link; every other ref target renders as a plain id span.
at: r.kind === "fact" ? link(r.target, "#/fact/" + encodeURIComponent(r.target), "id") : el("span", { class: "id", text: r.target })));

facts.text: fact writes the length of s.refs into the Refs heading and the length of s.inbound into the Inbound heading.
graphView mounts window.DossierGraph into a fresh div and returns graph.ready.
graphView titles the page Graph when an id is given and Subject tree when it is not.
route destroys an existing graph and clears the reference before it reads the location hash.
route splits the hash on slashes and decodes the joined remainder with decodeURIComponent.
route dispatches a first part of subject, fact, graph or search to that view and falls back to home for anything else.
route catches a failed view and replaces the page with an error paragraph holding e.message.
The window hashchange event is wired to route.
index.html loads /feed.js first, then /graph.js, then /app.js at the end of the body.
The header search box is id q with type search, the placeholder search facts and autofocus.
The g-feed f-line rule strips the button background and border and inherits the surrounding font.
at: .g-feed .f-line { background: none; border: 0; padding: 0; font: inherit; color: #05c; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; }

facts.text: The f-in animation of .35s is applied to f-new only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
The g-feed-list rule caps the list at max-height 120px and turns on overflow auto.
at: .g-feed-list { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; max-height: 120px; overflow: auto; }

facts.text: The g-panel rule fixes the side panel at 320px wide and gives it overflow auto.
at: .g-panel { width: 320px; overflow: auto; border: 1px solid #ddd; padding: 8px; }

facts.text: The g-stage rule takes the leftover flex space and paints it with the dark background #0e1116.
main is padded by 16px and capped at a max-width of 960px with auto side margins.
The header bar paints a #222 background with #eee text and the dossier link in #9cf.
at: header { padding: 10px 16px; background: #222; color: #eee; display: flex; gap: 12px; align-items: center; }

facts.text: The status badge is inline-block with a border radius of 8px and a 12px font on a #e8e8e8 background.
at: .status { display: inline-block; padding: 0 6px; border-radius: 8px; background: #e8e8e8; font-size: 12px; margin-left: 6px; }

facts.text: index.html sets the document title to the single word dossier.
entryForFact returns the indexed entry only while that entry is still present in rows, and deletes the index entry when it is not.
at: if (entry && rows.indexOf(entry) < 0) { delete factIndex[id]; entry = null; }

facts.text: lineText appends a plus sign and the ref count and the word refs to the base only when entry.refs is non-zero.
setLine stores lineText on entry.text and writes that string to entry.line when the element exists.
paint hides the empty message as soon as rows exist and hides the list while the strip is collapsed.
The inner el helper assigns its value through textContent only when the value is neither undefined nor null.
at: if (value !== undefined && value !== null) node.textContent = value;

facts.text: home shows each subject as a name link, a note holding its kind and fact count, and a graph link.
at: el("span", { class: "note", text: " " + s.kind + ", " + s.facts + " facts " }),

facts.text: subject titles the page Dossier plus the subject name, falling back to the id when d.subject is missing.
search writes the query and res.total into the Results for heading above the hit rows.
